title: Manchester City 1-1 Fulham: Anderson stunner halts Maresca's losing streak
subtitle: Manchester City were looking at a fourth straight defeat before Elliot Anderson's second-half strike earned them a point against Fulham.
paragraphs: Elliot Anderson's superb volley snapped Manchester City's Premier League losing streak as Enzo Maresca's team drew 1-1 with Fulham.

Having lost ground on leaders Arsenal at the top of the table, things did not start well for Man City at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday, with Rodrigo Muniz's curling effort handing Fulham a 16th-minute lead.
The home fans' mood soured when Erling Haaland saw an equaliser ruled out, but Anderson's volley restored parity just before the hour to ensure City avoided a fourth straight top-flight loss.
David Affengruber got in the way of shots from Haaland and Nico O'Reilly as City started on the front foot, but Fulham opened the scoring from their first attempt.
Former City winger Oscar Bobb surged down the flank from inside his own half before picking out Muniz, who whipped his shot into the top-right corner.
City thought they were back on level terms 24 minutes in when Haaland awkwardly directed Iliman Ndiaye's cross towards goal.
Bernd Leno got behind the initial shot before Haaland bundled it over the line, and it was disallowed as the goalkeeper was deemed to be in control of the ball before the follow-up.
Haaland then uncharacteristically blazed over the bar before City almost gifted Fulham a second when their backline switched off, but Gianluigi Donnarumma got behind Bobb's drilled strike.

Enzo Maresca's side got their reward for an improved second-half showing 57 minutes in when Anderson latched onto a half-cleared corner to volley home, bringing up his first league goal for City in spectacular fashion.
Anderson almost put City in front when Haaland pulled it back to him in the box, but he slid his low shot through Ryan Sessegnon's legs and wide of the far post.
Donnarumma was alert to deny both Muniz and Calvin Bassey at the end of quick Fulham counters, but despite late pressure from both sides, neither team could find a winner.
City's blushes spared as Fulham end long wait
Given City's drop in form before the international break, a match against Fulham would have been welcomed; they had won their last 17 Premier League games against them.

But City have now fallen 1-0 behind in four consecutive top-flight games for the first time since March/April 2012 (five). They have also conceded in nine consecutive games in all competitions for the first time since December 2019 (10).

Alvaro Arbeloa's decision to go with Muniz over Gonzalo Garcia proved to work, as the Brazilian has now scored in back-to-back league appearances for the first time since April 2025. He has now scored more goals in those two games (two) than he did in the whole of last season (one).

Maresca's side ultimately dominated the shot count, having 15 attempts worth 1.88 expected goals (xG) to Fulham's five, which were worth a combined 0.72 xG, but the visitors' defence stayed solid, and could only be breached by Anderson's moment of magic.
In fact, Arbeloa may feel they deserved more given they finished with more attempts on target (four to three) and caused City's defence real problems.
Fulham, though, have dropped 10 points from winning positions in the Premier League this season; only Brentford (11) have dropped more.

But Fulham still avoided defeat against City for the first time since September 2011 in all competitions, meaning the Citizens did not get the win they needed to leapfrog Brighton into second in the table.
